authority.legal_name: Kochi Water Metro — Kochi Metro Rail Limited (KMRL), a Government of Kerala / Government of India joint venture
authority.home_waters_label: the Kochi backwaters and Vembanad Lake

mandate.summary: The Kochi Water Metro, run by KMRL, is India's first integrated urban water-transport system — a fleet of battery-electric boats connecting ten islands around Kochi to the mainland and the Kochi Metro rail, ticketed on one card, with dozens more terminals and routes planned.
current_priorities: Connecting the Kochi islands to the mainland and the metro
Expanding to the full planned network of terminals and routes
Relieving the city's congested bridges and roads

policy_targets.vision: Kerala carbon-neutral / Kochi Water Metro master plan
policy_targets.decarb_note: The Kochi Water Metro is already all-electric — India's flagship zero-emission water-transport system — but the conventional displacement boats are slow, and only part of the planned 30-plus-terminal network is open.
policy_targets.relevance: Navier is the foiling upgrade to a network KMRL already runs all-electric — faster backwater lines that cover the same routes in a fraction of the time, extending Kochi's world-leading electric water-transport model rather than replacing it.

precedent.headline: The Kochi Water Metro is already India's model for public electric water transport.
precedent.network: KMRL runs the all-electric Kochi Water Metro from terminals including High Court, Vyttila, Vypin, Fort Kochi and Kakkanad — ten islands connected by battery boats, integrated with the Kochi Metro on one ticket, with the network expanding toward 38 terminals and 16 routes.
precedent.note: Public ferry service is core transport infrastructure here, not a novelty. Navier adds a fast passenger-only foiling layer on the busy corridors.

interpretation_for_navier: Navier is the foiling upgrade to a network KMRL already runs all-electric — faster backwater lines that cover the same routes in a fraction of the time, extending Kochi's world-leading electric water-transport model rather than replacing it.

regional_links.note: Domestic-only network across the Kochi backwaters and Vembanad Lake. Wider Kerala backwater links (Alappuzha/Kottayam) are secondary and out of scope for this phase.

routing_hazards.instruction: Every domestic leg must be routed through navigable open water with NO land crossings (interior_land_km == 0). Hand-curated waypoints required wherever a breakwater, barrier, bridge pier, reef, headland, naval/exclusion zone or shallows would otherwise be clipped. Use data-clean/uae_hand_waypoints.json format {from, to, waypoints:[[lng,lat]...]}.

hazards.detail: The Vembanad backwaters are shallow with shifting silt and seasonal water hyacinth — follow the dredged Water Metro channels and hand-waypoint around the shallows.
The backwaters carry dense local ferry and country-boat traffic — low-wake operation and geofenced no-foil zones at the jetties.
The Ernakulam/Willingdon Island reach crosses the Cochin Port shipping channel — cross at marked points clear of large vessels.
Backwater levels and currents swing sharply in the monsoon — routing must account for high-flow periods.
